25: let request schedule request =
26:   match request, schedule.pending with
27:   | Force, _ -> schedule.pending <- Some Force
28:   | Input, Some Force -> ()
29:   | Input, Some (Input | Background) | Input, None -> schedule.pending <- Some Input
30:   | Background, None -> schedule.pending <- Some Background
31:   | Background, Some (Input | Background | Force) -> ()
32: 
33: let deadline schedule =
34:   Option.map
35:     (fun rendered_at -> Int64.add rendered_at schedule.min_interval_ns)
36:     schedule.last_rendered_at_ns
37: 
38: let take ~input_pending schedule ~now_ns =
39:   let render () =
40:     schedule.pending <- None;
41:     schedule.last_rendered_at_ns <- Some now_ns;
42:     Render
43:   in
44:   match schedule.pending with
45:   | None -> Idle
46:   | Some Force -> render ()
47:   | Some Input when not input_pending -> render ()
48:   | Some (Input | Background) ->
49:     (* Available input can still be combined. A continuous stream keeps the
50:        frame interval; once it drains, the branch above presents its result
51:        without waiting for more input that may never arrive. *)
52:     match deadline schedule with
53:     | Some due when Int64.compare now_ns due < 0 ->
54:         Wait_until due
55:     | None | Some _ -> render ()
56: 
57: let input_timeout_seconds schedule ~now_ns ~maximum =
58:   let maximum = max 0.0 maximum in
59:   match schedule.pending with
60:   | None -> maximum
61:   | Some (Force | Input) -> 0.0
62:   | Some Background ->
63:     (match deadline schedule with
64:      | None -> 0.0
65:      | Some due ->
66:        let remaining_ns = Int64.sub due now_ns in
67:        if Int64.compare remaining_ns 0L <= 0 then 0.0
68:        else min maximum (Int64.to_float remaining_ns /. 1_000_000_000.0))

136: (* Both sources can hold bytes already read from the terminal. A character
137:    the decoder holds is awaiting more input, so it must not defer a frame. *)
138: let input_reader_has_pending_bytes reader =
139:   (not (Queue.is_empty reader.queued))
140:   || reader.position < reader.filled
141:   || match reader.terminal_probe with
142:      | None -> false
143:      | Some decoder -> Masc_tui_terminal_probe.has_replay decoder
144: 
145: (* Whether the terminal has bytes for us, waited for inside Eio rather than
146:    in the kernel.
147: 
148:    [Unix.select] blocks the whole domain, not one fiber. Every fiber waiting
149:    on a socket then advances only when this loop comes back round, so a reply
150:    costs the number of steps it takes times what one pass of the loop costs.
151:    That is how a request the server answers in milliseconds reached the
152:    ten-second timeout: measured with masc-http-probe, the same 1.8 MB read
153:    takes 5.5 seconds beside a loop that waits this way and 26 ms beside one
154:    that waits through Eio (RFC-0429 §3.0). Waiting through Eio takes this
155:    fiber out of the run queue, and those fibers run until they block in turn.
156: 
157:    Only the readiness wait races the deadline. The read below is never
158:    cancelled, so no keystroke is taken from the terminal and then dropped
159:    with the losing fiber -- which is what racing the read itself would risk.
160: 
161:    A wait with no time left has nothing to register: asking Eio for one would
162:    cancel it in the same breath, and the kernel answers that question without
163:    blocking anyway. *)
164: let terminal_has_bytes ~remaining =
165:   let kernel_wait seconds =
166:     match Unix.select [ Unix.stdin ] [] [] seconds with
167:     | ready, _, _ -> ready <> []
168:   in
169:   if remaining <= 0.0 then kernel_wait 0.0
170:   else
171:     match (Eio_guard.is_eio_fiber (), Eio_context.get_clock_opt ()) with
172:     | true, Some clock ->
173:         Eio.Fiber.first
174:           (fun () ->
175:             Eio_unix.await_readable Unix.stdin;
176:             true)
177:           (fun () ->
178:             Eio.Time.sleep clock remaining;
179:             false)
180:     | true, None | false, _ ->
181:         (* The startup terminal probe reads through this same reader from
182:            inside [Eio_guard.run_in_systhread], where an Eio effect has no
183:            handler. The kernel wait is the right one there for the same
184:            reason the probe runs on a thread at all: blocking a system
185:            thread does not stop the domain. *)
186:         kernel_wait remaining
187: 
188: (* A read buffer can end while the next chunk already waits in the kernel.
189:    Include readiness without consuming input, so a long burst is coalesced
190:    across buffer boundaries too. EINTR means readiness was not observed;
191:    defer at most to the existing frame deadline and let the reader retry. *)
192: let input_reader_has_ready_input reader =
193:   match reader.probe_preparation with
194:   | Some _ -> false
195:   | None -> input_reader_has_pending_bytes reader
196:     || try terminal_has_bytes ~remaining:0.0 with
197:        | Unix.Unix_error (Unix.EINTR, _, _) -> true

448: (** Read one key, one paste, or one thing the terminal said back. *)
449: let read_available_input ~timeout reader () : input_event option =
450:   (* The reader belongs to this fiber. Keeping it here lets readiness use
451:      [await_readable] and the Eio timer; moving the whole decoder to a system
452:      thread also moves buffered keys and every frame-deadline poll there.
453:      Only readiness races the timer: the consuming Unix.read stays after it. *)
454:   Eio_guard.with_named_switch "tui-read-key" (fun () ->
455:       let enqueue decoded =
456:         List.iter
457:           (fun event -> Queue.add event reader.queued)
458:           decoded
459:       in
460:       (* Queued events only; an empty queue is the answer, not a reason to
461:          read again. *)
462:       let rec drain () =
463:         match Queue.take_opt reader.queued with
464:         | None -> None
465:         | Some decoded -> (
466:             match input_event_of_decoded reader decoded with
467:             | Some event -> Some event
468:             | None -> drain ())
469:       in
470:       let rec serve () =
471:         match Queue.take_opt reader.queued with
472:         | Some decoded -> (
473:             match input_event_of_decoded reader decoded with
474:             | Some event -> Some event
475:             | None -> serve ())
476:         | None -> read ()
477:       and read () =
478:         let wait =
479:           match Masc_tui_input_decoder.pending reader.decoder with
480:           (* Not bounded by [timeout]: a frame due now passes 0, and a prefix
481:              given no time ends as Escape, splitting an arrow into three keys. *)
482:           | Some Masc_tui_input_decoder.Prefix -> sequence_byte_wait_seconds
483:           | Some (Masc_tui_input_decoder.Sequence | Masc_tui_input_decoder.Character) ->
484:               Float.min timeout sequence_byte_wait_seconds
485:           | Some (Masc_tui_input_decoder.Pasting | Masc_tui_input_decoder.Draining)
486:           | None ->
487:               timeout
488:         in
489:         match take_input_byte reader ~timeout:wait with
490:         | None ->
491:             enqueue (Masc_tui_input_decoder.idle reader.decoder);
492:             drain ()
493:         | Some byte ->
494:             let was_in_paste = in_paste reader in
495:             let was_pasting =
496:               Masc_tui_input_decoder.pending reader.decoder
497:               = Some Masc_tui_input_decoder.Pasting
498:             in
499:             enqueue (Masc_tui_input_decoder.feed reader.decoder byte);
500:             (match paste_phase reader with
501:              | Pasting clock when not was_pasting ->
502:                  clock.last_byte_ns <- Mtime_clock.elapsed_ns ();
503:                  clock.cancel_armed <- false
504:              | Pasting clock | Draining_tail clock ->
505:                  clock.last_byte_ns <- Mtime_clock.elapsed_ns ()
506:              | No_paste -> ());
507:             if not (Queue.is_empty reader.queued) then serve ()
508:             else if was_in_paste && not (in_paste reader) then
509:               (* The end marker of a drained tail: nothing to hand on, and the
510:                  caller notices the guard lifting. *)
511:               None
512:             else if in_paste reader && reader.position >= reader.filled then
513:               (* Return to the main loop after each terminal read buffer. A
514:                  sender that never pauses must not hold Ctrl-C or other queued
515:                  work behind this loop. *)
516:               None
517:             else read ()
518:       in
519:       let event = serve () in
520:       Option.iter (fun event -> Option.iter
521:         (fun kind -> observe_installed reader (Startup.First_input_decoded kind)) (input_kind event)) event;
522:       event)
523: 
524: let read_input ?(timeout = 0.1) reader () : input_event option =
525:   match reader.probe_preparation with
526:   | Some preparation -> preparation.wait ~timeout; None
527:   | None -> read_available_input ~timeout reader ()

61: val present :
62:   t ->
63:   ?force_present:bool ->
64:   invalidate_before:bool ->
65:   write:(string -> unit) ->
66:   flush:(unit -> unit) ->
67:   frame ->
68:   present_result
69: (** Present one fixed-viewport frame with at most one [write] and one [flush].
70:     [invalidate_before] discards the cached screen before comparison, coupling
71:     out-of-band terminal writes to the next full redraw.
72:     [force_present] asks for a full redraw only if rows and cursor would
73:     otherwise be unchanged, so changed input authority can be presented
74:     without turning ordinary differential updates into full redraws.
75:     Content updates compare opaque ANSI rows byte-for-byte. Cursor-only moves
76:     remain differential and are emitted in the same atomic output buffer.
77:     [Presented] means the terminal accepted output for this frame, and says
78:     which rows it wrote;
79:     [Unchanged] means no bytes were necessary, so semantic input authority
80:     must remain with the last frame that was actually emitted. *)

262: let present presenter ?(force_present = false) ~invalidate_before ~write ~flush (frame : frame) =
263:   if invalidate_before then invalidate presenter;
264:   let terminal_rows = max 1 frame.terminal_rows in
265:   let terminal_cols = max 1 frame.terminal_cols in
266:   let cursor_changed =
267:     match presenter.previous with
268:     | None -> true
269:     | Some previous -> previous.cursor <> frame.cursor
270:   in
271:   let full_redraw =
272:     presenter.invalidated
273:     ||
274:     match presenter.previous with
275:     | None -> true
276:     | Some previous -> not (same_geometry previous frame)
277:   in
278:   let unchanged =
279:     (not full_redraw)
280:     && (not cursor_changed)
281:     && (match presenter.previous with
282:         | Some previous ->
283:             lines_equal_to_screen frame.lines previous.screen ~terminal_rows
284:         | None -> false)
285:   in
286:   if unchanged && not force_present then
287:     Unchanged
288:   else begin
289:     let full_redraw = full_redraw || unchanged in
290:     let screen = screen_of_frame frame in
291:     let prev_screen =
292:       match presenter.previous with
293:       | Some previous -> Some previous.screen
294:       | None -> None
295:     in
296:     let buffer = presenter.output_buffer in
297:     Buffer.clear buffer;
298:     if presenter.synchronized_output then
299:       Buffer.add_string buffer begin_synchronized_output;
300:     (* Once at the start of every frame written here, and nowhere else the
301:        presenter writes: the request probe counts written frames by it
302:        (scripts/harness/perf/tui_request_surfaces.py). The machine screen
303:        opens each of its batches with it too, and frame timing records those
304:        batches as frames of their own. *)
305:     Buffer.add_string buffer disable_autowrap;
306:     if full_redraw then Buffer.add_string buffer clear_screen;
307:     let repaint =
308:       match prev_screen with
309:       | Some prev when not full_redraw ->
310:           let rewritten = ref [] in
311:           for row = 0 to terminal_rows - 1 do
312:             if not (String.equal prev.(row) screen.(row)) then begin
313:               append_row buffer row screen.(row);
314:               rewritten := row :: !rewritten
315:             end
316:           done;
317:           Rows (List.rev !rewritten)
318:       | _ ->
319:           for row = 0 to terminal_rows - 1 do
320:             append_row buffer row screen.(row)
321:           done;
322:           Whole_screen
323:     in
324:     append_cursor buffer ~terminal_rows ~terminal_cols frame.cursor;
325:     Buffer.add_string buffer enable_autowrap;
326:     if presenter.synchronized_output then
327:       Buffer.add_string buffer end_synchronized_output;
328:     let output = Buffer.contents buffer in
329:     let snapshot =
330:       { surface_key = frame.surface_key;
331:         compact_frame = frame.compact_frame;
332:         terminal_rows;
333:         terminal_cols;
334:         cursor = frame.cursor;
335:         screen;
336:       }
337:     in
338:     (try
339:        write output;
340:        flush ();
341:        presenter.previous <- Some snapshot;
342:        presenter.invalidated <- false;
343:        Presented repaint
344:      with exn ->
345:        presenter.invalidated <- true;
346:        raise exn)
347:   end

649: let time_present ~tag ~write ~flush f =
650:   if not enabled then f ~write ~flush
651:   else begin
652:     let write_ns = ref 0L and flush_ns = ref 0L in
653:     let bytes = ref 0 and writes = ref 0 and flushes = ref 0 in
654:     let timed_write text =
655:       let started = Mtime_clock.elapsed_ns () in
656:       write text;
657:       let elapsed = Int64.sub (Mtime_clock.elapsed_ns ()) started in
658:       write_ns := Int64.add !write_ns elapsed;
659:       bytes := !bytes + String.length text;
660:       incr writes
661:     in
662:     let timed_flush () =
663:       let started = Mtime_clock.elapsed_ns () in
664:       flush ();
665:       let elapsed = Int64.sub (Mtime_clock.elapsed_ns ()) started in
666:       flush_ns := Int64.add !flush_ns elapsed;
667:       incr flushes
668:     in
669:     let started = Mtime_clock.elapsed_ns () in
670:     let result = f ~write:timed_write ~flush:timed_flush in
671:     let completed_ns = Mtime_clock.elapsed_ns () in
672:     samples := Samples.add_timed !samples Present ~tag:(Some tag)
673:       ~started_ns:started ~completed_ns ~home_questions:None
674:       ~output:(Some { write_ns = !write_ns; flush_ns = !flush_ns;
675:                 bytes = !bytes; writes = !writes; flushes = !flushes });
676:     result
677:   end
